findings.finding: Shared-boundary comparison already included deadlines, but it did not explicitly challenge separately accepted local retry/timeout policies against one end-to-end time/load contract.
findings.consequence: The composed decision could inherit a false request bound or overlook layered downstream amplification even when every individual loop is bounded.
findings.correction: Trace actual gateway/client/SDK policies and sequential/parallel paths, reconcile remaining budget and total attempts, identify policy ownership, and verify downstream calls/residual work for one logical request.

findings.finding: The new composition question needs bounded specialist ownership without turning this coordinator skill into a timeout/retry implementation guide.
findings.correction: Route remaining-budget behavior to timeouts-and-deadlines and attempt location/eligibility to retries-and-backoff; add only a suggests entry for the latter.

sources.supports: Independent layered retries multiply attempts/load; choosing a retry location has a work-efficiency trade-off. Used as mechanism evidence, not a universal retry policy.
Independent deployability, business capability organization, remote-call/failure costs and explicit limits of a conformance definition; supports preserved role/scope.

limits: No runnable microservice application was supplied; changes are architecture guidance and a specialist routing addition.
No live or simulated service integration, load, cancellation-propagation or independent agent evaluation was executed.
The two cases are synthetic development fixtures, not unseen holdouts or measured improvement.
A configuration-level attempt bound does not prove transport behavior, production latency, capacity or safe cancellation; the skill requires the relevant path evidence.
The gRPC source demonstrates a mechanism; it does not establish automatic propagation for an arbitrary HTTP/client stack.

taskInput.task: Review the supplied checkout architecture artifacts and update decisions.md: reconcile affected guarantees and owners, preserve unaffected accepted decisions, and define the smallest useful integration check. Do not change production configuration or introduce a new service/framework.

files.call-path.md: Synthetic review fixture. One incoming read-only quote request enters Edge, which calls Checkout, which calls Pricing. Calls and retries are sequential; no fan-out, hedging, event replay or additional client retry layer exists. Every Edge attempt invokes a fresh Checkout operation. Every Checkout operation invokes Pricing using its configured SDK policy. A terminal retryable Pricing failure becomes a retryable Checkout failure. The outer operation preserves one 500ms deadline at every hop. maxAttempts includes the original call. Every retry checks remaining time; all sleeps fit inside that same deadline.
files.failure-fixture.md: The candidate failure fixture makes every Pricing call return retryable 503 after 5ms. Each retry layer waits 10ms between attempts. There is no successful branch in this fixture. Use these values for a configuration-level walkthrough; no actual service test result has been supplied.
files.requirements.md: The accepted resource contract permits at most three Pricing calls per one incoming quote request, across all components. The request deadline is 500ms, including waits/retries; production latency is not yet validated. The operation is read-only and repetition-safe. Edge owns its outbound retry policy; Checkout owns the Pricing SDK policy. The Checkout product owner owns the end-to-end request contract. The architecture lead resolves conflicting policies. Existing tenant authorization at Pricing has separate passing evidence and is unchanged.
files.decisions.md:
D1: Edge's configured retry policy is accepted locally; validation of its own loop completed.
D2: Checkout's configured Pricing SDK retry policy is accepted locally; validation of its own loop completed.
D3: Proposed composition claim: local loop limits satisfy the accepted end-to-end Pricing attempt cap. Integrated failure validation remains open.
D4: Accepted tenant authorization at Pricing; existing test evidence covers the unchanged path.
Next slice: pending integration review.

expected: Identify nine possible Pricing calls for the logical request in this configured fixture, violating the accepted cap of three; distinguish this inference from an executed trace.

Update affected D1/D2/D3 relationships and send the joint budget/ownership question to the named authority; propose a bounded correction such as one retry location or a shared cap, with its efficiency trade-off.
Preserve D4 and the existing process boundaries. Define a fault check counting Pricing calls per logical request and checking remaining deadline/residual work.
failureConditions: Conclude total attempts are three merely because each local policy is bounded.
Add the loop counts to obtain six, or count maxAttempts as retries plus an initial fourth call.
Claim local unit tests prove the composition or a new circuit breaker/mesh automatically repairs it.
Reopen unrelated domain/data/security decisions without evidence.
